neighbours.label: the place or group someone leaves, flees or is forced out of (the object of leave / flee / exit from)
fire: After the scandal broke, the coach was forced to resign and leave the sport.
Rising rents have pushed many young families to leave the area for good.
The rebels were driven back and had to flee from the capital overnight.
Thousands of workers left the industry after the factories closed down.
During the war her grandparents escaped from the country with nothing.
He felt bitter about the way he was pushed out of the company he founded.
Many teachers have quit the profession because of low pay and long hours.
The young prince was exiled and forced to flee from his homeland.
quiet: After the scandal broke, the coach was asked to speak about the sport.
Rising rents have made many young families think hard about the area.
The rebels were driven back and had to regroup near the capital overnight.
Thousands of workers joined the industry after the new factories opened.
During the war her grandparents stayed in the country and kept farming.
He felt proud about the way he had built up the company he founded.
Many teachers have praised the profession despite low pay and long hours.
The young prince was crowned and returned in triumph to his homeland.

short: what one is forced to leave
